metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness writes a durable error turn boundary for failed model calls, and the DSH adapter maps that boundary to a sticky terminal session error.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 has an explicit failed-turn outcome. The installed `dsh-agent-loop` catches every non-cancellation error from a model step, converts an `LlmError` to its structured failure, and appends `turn/end` from a `finally` block with `reason.kind=error`. This is the agent's durable failure boundary, not an inference from a completed turn. A measured local v3 transcript confirms the emitted shape for a real failed LM Studio request: `turn/start`, `request/context` naming `qwen/qwen3.5-9b`, an assistant attempt ending with `PI_AI_ERROR`, then `turn/end` with `reason.kind=error`, the same code, and the error message. A second measured failure carries `MISSING_CREDENTIAL`. The TUI renderer also has a dedicated red error branch for this record.

The DSH adapter handles that exact durable record. `parseTurnEnd` always emits `turn_done`; when `reason.kind` is `error`, it also creates a terminal `SessionError`, lowercases the agent error code, and preserves the message. `TestParserMapsTerminalError` uses the timestamp and shape from the measured `MISSING_CREDENTIAL` record. The tailer records an error after applying any turn-boundary clear, so an event that contains both the failed boundary and the error remains failed. Terminal errors are not cleared by their own turn boundary. The classifier's `session_error` rule routes the session to `error`, and `classifyAgentDone` independently returns `error` if a turn boundary and error reach the same classification path. The daemon therefore resolves the failed turn immediately and does not leave it in `working`.

This DSH-specific final state differs from the scenario's older generic `ready -> working -> ready` wording. Returning this session to `ready` would hide a structured terminal failure that DSH explicitly persisted. The current four-state daemon contract uses `error` for that signal and clears it only when the user starts a later turn. The expected spec therefore asserts `ready -> working -> error` and a 10-second error hold. The committed muse cell for this scenario uses the same evidence-based deviation for an agent that also emits a structured terminal failure.

The driver implements `send`, `wait_turn`, and `sleep`. Its `wait_turn` counts every durable `turn/end`, including an error boundary. Its temporary provider patch already exposes `base_url` and `api_key`, so the recipe can point the validly-authenticated OpenAI-compatible route at an unused loopback port. That produces a provider connection failure without changing the installed profile or consuming model tokens. The 300-second budget follows the other DSH model-turn cells and exceeds the measured 2m38s local Qwen turn if the trigger is accidentally bypassed. The 15-second post-boundary hold matches the longest ordinary sibling settle window; Hermes' 120-second sleep is specific to its four-continuation trigger and does not transfer because DSH's configured route has no retry policy.

The model is pinned because `request/context` is written before the failure and the recipe selects `qwen/qwen3.5-9b`. Cost and tokens are expected to remain zero because the connection fails before an assistant completion or usage record is produced.
caveats: Vacuous-pass check: the lifecycle spec could pass on a different terminal failure before DSH reaches the dead endpoint, such as a missing credential or malformed provider profile. The recipe therefore supplies a non-empty mock API key, requires the selected loopback port to have no listener, and requires recording review to confirm the durable error message names a connection or transport failure.
Load-bearing environment precondition: no process may listen on 127.0.0.1:18804 during the recording. Re-probe the port immediately before record; do not trust this assessment-time state.

The exact measured DSH failure records are credential failures, not connection refusals. The installed agent-loop source proves that all non-cancellation model errors use the same `turn/end` error boundary, but the connection-refused wording and code remain provisional until record confirms them.
The scenario text says no normal turn-end signal is emitted. DSH emits an abnormal `turn/end` whose reason is explicitly `error`; the adapter must not collapse this into a successful ready state.

A very fast connection refusal can place `turn/start` and `turn/end` close together. The DSH writer appends the start before making the request, and the daemon's first activity edge is immediate, but the live recording must confirm that the user-visible working phase is not coalesced away.

The model observation is expected from `request/context`, which precedes both measured failures. Tokens and cost are asserted zero for the failed turn. If the installed TUI issues an unrelated title-model request that produces usage, record must correct only those observation fields and keep the failure arc unchanged.
The driver uses a fresh per-run cwd and pre-launch marker. Without that isolation, another DSH transcript could satisfy the state phases and the cell would prove nothing about the driven session.

sources.note: Measured failed LM Studio turn: turn/start; request/context for qwen/qwen3.5-9b; assistant attempt finish.kind=error with PI_AI_ERROR; step/end; then turn/end reason.kind=error with the same failure. No normal assistant completion exists.
Second measured failed turn with MISSING_CREDENTIAL. Its turn/end timestamp and payload are the source shape pinned by the adapter test.
Installed 0.1.5-rc.2 runtime: the turn loop catches every non-aborted error, records an LlmError failure as reason.kind=error, and appends turn/end in finally.
The installed TUI has a dedicated turn/end reason.kind=error rendering branch, confirming this is a first-class failed-turn outcome.
parseTurnEnd maps error boundaries to turn_done plus a terminal SessionError whose class and message come from the durable DSH failure.
TestParserMapsTerminalError pins the measured MISSING_CREDENTIAL shape; compressed end-to-end coverage exercises the v3 source.
applySessionError clears before recording a same-event failure, so turn_done plus terminal error remains sticky; only a later recovery turn clears it.
SessionError.ClearedByTurnBoundary excludes terminal failures because the boundary is the failed turn's own epilogue.
The session_error rule and classifyAgentDone both route a standing SessionError to the canonical error state.
Implements send, wait_turn, and sleep; applies base_url/api_key through a temporary patch; wait_turn delegates to the durable turn counter.
Counts all durable turn/end records, so an error boundary releases wait_turn without confusing it with a successful completion.

preconditions: dsh >=0.1.5-rc.2 is installed and on PATH
the community TUI profile is installed under ~/.dsh/profiles/tui
127.0.0.1:18804 has no listener immediately before recording; re-probe it at record time
irrlichd is recording the deepseek-harness adapter
setup: The interactive driver creates a fresh cwd under the staging directory and launches `dsh --profile tui` in tmux.
The driver applies a temporary patch that selects the OpenAI-compatible LM Studio route and qwen/qwen3.5-9b without modifying the installed TUI profile.
The patch supplies a non-empty recording-only API key but points base_url at the deliberately unused loopback port 18804, so the model request fails at transport time.
The driver resolves the post-marker compressed transcript by header cwd and waits for the durable error turn/end count.

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: the post-marker DSH session is born in ready and binds its session.lock writer PID
the user prompt moves the same session to working
the durable transcript contains turn/end with reason.kind=error and a connection or transport failure message after the real user message
the same session transitions from working to error and remains there for at least 10 seconds without entering waiting or returning to ready
the replay summary reports model qwen/qwen3.5-9b with zero cumulative tokens and cost for the failed request
recipe.scope_note: Uses a 15-second post-error window, matching the longest ordinary sibling settle delay. Hermes' 120-second sleep covers its agent-specific continuation ladder and does not apply because this DSH provider profile has no retry policy.
